angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 604,285 km at 169.89 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.8863 +/- 0.0105 mas (same row, RUWE 0.94): 169.89 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.8686 +/- 0.0133 solar radii from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1248 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract): 604,285 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.9042 +/- 0.0273 solar masses from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1248 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5205 +/- 56 K from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1248 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1248 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1248.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.517, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
